description: Insights M1: ship the /insights Signal Summary skeleton (four verdict sentences) plus the only new backend capability — each of the four metrics surfaces (completion, delivery-time, quality, agent-cost) returns a current window and an adjacent previous window of equal length so the frontend derives a trend arrow and magnitude in a single read. All four backend changes are strictly additive; no schema migration, no API contract break.

tasks.title: Completion surface: dual-window totals + SampleCount discriminator + inject TimeProvider
tasks.description: Add a current-window total and a previous-adjacent-window total (each: completed + failed counts) to the completion surface response DTO and IssueQuerier.GetCompletionBucketsAsync, both anchored on terminal-event time using the latest-terminal-event classification. Introduce a SampleCount (terminal-issue count) on the new totals object so a zero-sample window is distinguishable from a genuine zero-completion window. Switch the completion route handler (IssueRoutes.Metrics.cs) from DateTimeOffset.UtcNow to the DI-registered TimeProvider so the new previous-window branch is deterministically testable. Strictly additive: existing per-bucket series, window bounds, and bucket granularity are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Response DTO gains a current-window total {completed, failed, sampleCount} and a previous-adjacent-window total of the same shape
Previous window is [now-2W, now-W] (W = current 30d day-window / 12wk week-window), same length as current, advances with current time, uses identical latest-terminal-event classification
A zero-sample window (no terminal issues) yields SampleCount==0 and is distinguishable from a genuine zero-completion window (SampleCount>0, completed==0)
Completion route handler resolves TimeProvider from DI and calls timeProvider.GetUtcNow() instead of DateTimeOffset.UtcNow (mirrors IssueRoutes.DeliveryTimeMetrics.cs)
Existing Buckets, Window {from,to}, and fixed day/week granularity are preserved unchanged; existing fields are not removed or re-shaped
Unsupported bucket value is still rejected with 'unsupported_bucket'; unknown project still returns 404
API spec (IssueMetricsApiSpecs) covers: both-window totals from seeded events, previous-window empty result vs genuine zero, totals additive to existing response

Querier spec (IssueQuerierSpecs) covers: previous-window length/adjacency, latest-terminal-event dedup across windows, zero-sample vs genuine-zero discrimination, driven by an explicit DateTimeOffset now
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors
tasks.output: Modified IssueRoutes.Metrics.cs, IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs (completion totals DTO), IssueQuerier.cs (GetCompletionBucketsAsync); new + extended tests in IssueMetricsApiSpecs.cs and IssueQuerierSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: Includes the D4 opportunistic TimeProvider injection fix — it is required to test the new previous-window logic without a real clock; do not split it into a separate task. Querier already accepts DateTimeOffset now as a parameter, so only the route layer needs the DI swap.

tasks.title: Delivery-time surface: previous-adjacent-window average cycle time
tasks.description: Add a previous-adjacent-window average cycle time (double?, null ⟹ no delivered issues) to the delivery-time surface, computed over [now-2W, now-W] using the identical earliest-work-start-to-final-completion (surviving retries) definition and completion-time windowing the current window already uses. Strictly additive: the existing per-issue Points series and fixed 30-day trailing window are unchanged; only the previous-window average is added.
acceptanceCriteria: Response DTO gains a previous-window average cycle time as a nullable double (null ⟹ no delivered issues in that window), mirroring the existing nullable CycleDays 'undefined' idiom
Previous window is [now-2W, now-W] (W = existing 30-day window), uses the same cycle-time definition and CompletedAt-anchored windowing as the current window
When the previous window has no delivered issues, its average is the defined empty result (null), distinguishable from a genuine zero-duration average, evaluated independently of the current window
Existing Points series, fixed trailing window, and existing empty-result semantics are preserved unchanged
API spec (IssueMetricsApiSpecs) covers: both-window averages returned, empty previous window independent of current, additive preservation of existing response
Querier spec (IssueQuerierSpecs) covers: previous-window adjacency/length and identical cycle-time definition, driven by an explicit DateTimeOffset now
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors
tasks.output: Modified IssueRoutes.DeliveryTimeMetrics.cs, IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs (delivery-time DTO), IssueQuerier.cs (GetDeliveryTimesAsync); new + extended tests in IssueMetricsApiSpecs.cs and IssueQuerierSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: TimeProvider is already injected on this route; no clock fix needed. The route already calls timeProvider.GetUtcNow().

tasks.title: Quality surface: previous-adjacent-window first-time-right rate
tasks.description: Add a previous-adjacent-window first-time-right rate (with SampleCount, reusing the surface's existing SampleCount + nullable-rate empty idiom) to the AI-quality surface, computed over the 30-day window [now-60d, now-30d] using the identical ship-time windowing and first-time-right classification (a shipped issue is FTR iff no check across its whole lifecycle triggered a repair). Strictly additive: the existing window7d/window30d single-point rates, per-stage rework rates, and per-bucket trend series are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Response DTO gains a previous-window first-time-right rate plus its SampleCount (SampleCount==0 ⟹ no shipped issues ⟹ empty, distinguishable from a genuine rate of 0 or 1)
Previous window is the same length as the current 30-day window and immediately precedes it, using identical ship-time windowing and FTR classification
Empty previous window is evaluated independently of the current window and is distinguishable from a genuine rate
Existing window7d, window30d, per-stage rework rates, and per-bucket trend series are preserved unchanged
API spec (IssueMetricsApiSpecs) covers: both-window rates returned, empty previous window independent of current and distinguishable from genuine 0/1, additive preservation of existing response
Querier spec (IssueQuerierSpecs) covers: previous-window adjacency/length and identical FTR classification, driven by an explicit DateTimeOffset now
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors
tasks.output: Modified IssueRoutes.QualityMetrics.cs, IssueRoutes.Dtos.cs (quality DTO), IssueQuerier.cs (GetQualityAsync); new + extended tests in IssueMetricsApiSpecs.cs and IssueQuerierSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: Per design D1, the trend basis is the existing window30d (current) plus a previous 30d window; the 7d window stays untouched for other consumers. TimeProvider is already injected on this route.

tasks.title: Agent-cost surface: windowed current + previous spend and per-issue cost
tasks.description: Add a windowed current-window and previous-adjacent-window spend (sum of in-window per-session UsageSummary.CostAmount for sessions whose creation time falls in the window) and per-issue cost (window spend / count of issues completed in the window) to the agent-cost surface, distinct from the existing cumulative rollup. Both windows are 30 days and advance with the current time. Each metric's emptiness is evaluated independently per window: no sessions ⟹ empty spend; no completed issues ⟹ empty per-issue cost. Strictly additive: the existing cumulative totalCost/todayCost/doneIssuesCount/costPerShip rollup and 7-day usage timeseries are unchanged. Reuse the existing AgentCostMetricDto {amount, currency, sampleCount} empty idiom (amount null ⟹ empty, distinct from genuine 0.0).
acceptanceCriteria: Response DTO gains current-window and previous-window figures, each: spend {amount, currency, sampleCount} and per-issue cost {amount, currency, sampleCount}, using the existing AgentCostMetricDto shape
Windowed spend = sum of per-session CostAmount over sessions created in the window; per-issue cost = window spend / in-window completed-issue count
Previous window is the same length (30d) as and immediately precedes the current window; both advance with the current time
No-sessions window ⟹ empty spend (amount null, sampleCount 0); no-completed-issues window ⟹ empty per-issue cost; the two emptiness states are evaluated independently per metric per window
Genuine-zero spend (amount 0.0, sampleCount>0) is distinguishable from empty spend, consistent with GetCost_FreeShippingIsRealZeroNotEmpty
Existing cumulative rollup (totalCost/todayCost/doneIssuesCount/costPerShip) and 7-day usage timeseries are preserved unchanged

API spec (AgentCostRollupApiSpecs) covers: windowed spend/per-issue-cost for both windows, independent emptiness per metric, additive preservation of cumulative rollup, genuine-zero vs empty distinction
If windowing logic is added to AgentSessionQuerier, add querier-level specs mirroring the Issue querier-spec pattern (currently cost has API-level specs only)
`npm test` (server) passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors
tasks.output: Modified AgentRoutes.cs (/agent/cost handler), AgentSessionReadModels.cs (DTO), AgentSessionQuerier.cs (windowing); new + extended tests in AgentCostRollupApiSpecs.cs (and a new querier spec if logic moves into the querier)
tasks.notes: TimeProvider is injected into AgentSessionQuerier via constructor (not the route handler); reuse Now() from the querier. The completed-issue count per window can be derived from the same terminal-event classification used by the completion surface. This is the only surface introducing a brand-new windowed figure (not just a previous mirror of an existing window).

tasks.title: Insights Signal Summary page: route, nav, verdict-derivation model, and components
tasks.description: Add the project-scoped /insights route and an 'Insights' sidebar nav entry, the pages/insights FSD slice with a pure model/ verdict-derivation layer (no React: a Verdict discriminated union {kind:'full'|'currentOnly'|'insufficient'} plus direction/magnitude/tolerance/polarity rules per dimension) and a SignalSummary component rendering exactly four verdicts (产出节奏/交付效率/质量信号/投入信号) plus a ChartPlaceholder zone marked for M2. Extend the four existing hooks' TS interfaces (CompletionTrendResponse, DeliveryTimeMetricsResponse, QualityMetricsResponse, AgentCostRollupDto) with the optional previous-window fields from T-001..T-004. Compose the existing hooks (useCompletionThroughput, useDeliveryTime, useQualityMetrics, useCostRollup, useStageDuration) — no new hooks, no new query keys. Copy is hardcoded inline (no i18n exists).
acceptanceCriteria: /insights route renders InsightsPage inside the existing /:projectName layout; sidebar shows an 'Insights' nav entry (data-testid 'nav-insights') that navigates to /insights via useProjectPath; the Dashboard route and content remain unchanged and reachable
SignalSummary renders exactly four verdict sentences (throughput, delivery, quality, investment), conclusions first; no fifth dimension and no dimension omitted; no migrated Dashboard chart
Each verdict shows current-window value + trend direction (↑/↓/持平) + change magnitude derived strictly from current-vs-previous-window comparison; a trend is never derived from a single window

Direction/magnitude/polarity rules per design D6: throughput = count delta (↑ favorable); delivery = relative % change (↓ favorable/faster); quality = percentage-point delta (↑ favorable); investment = relative % change per metric (↓ favorable/cheaper). Doubles use a relative tolerance floor for 持平 to avoid float-jitter arrows

Throughput verdict derives counts from completion current/previous totals; delivery verdict names the slowest stage (max non-null AverageSeconds from the existing stage-duration surface) and omits it when no stage samples exist (D3 — no new endpoint)
Quality verdict derives pp delta from quality current/previous FTR rates; investment verdict derives spend and per-issue-cost trends independently from agent-cost windowed figures
Each verdict degrades independently and gracefully: no previous window ⟹ hide trend/magnitude (current-only); no current-window samples ⟹ '数据不足'; never renders a misleading arrow, never errors
ChartPlaceholder zone is present below the summary and visibly marked as a future deliverable (e.g. '图表将在后续迁移'), rendering no chart

model/ pure functions are unit-tested (.test.ts, sub-50ms, no React render) covering all four dimensions, direction/magnitude/tolerance, polarity, and each degradation branch (no baseline, no current samples, independent per verdict)
InsightsPage.test.tsx (.test.tsx, jsdom) covers: page renders, four verdicts present, trend arrows for a populated project, graceful degradation / empty-state, slowest-stage omission
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass
tasks.output: New pages/insights/ slice (ui/InsightsPage.tsx + InsightsPage.test.tsx, model/*.ts + *.test.ts, SignalSummary + ChartPlaceholder components, index.ts); route + import added to app/App.tsx; nav entry added to widgets/app-shell/ui/AppSidebar.tsx; optional previous-window fields added to the four metrics TS interfaces in entities/issue + entities/agent
tasks.notes: The frontend consumes the enriched DTOs from all four backend tasks, so it depends on all of them. The four TS interface extensions are additive optional fields, so the page can be built/tested with mocks even before backend merge, but the feature is only complete with real dual-window data flowing. Per D5, keep all delta/direction/degradation/polarity logic in pure model/ functions (trivially unit-testable); components must not branch on SampleCount directly. a11y specs (tests/a11y/) are optional/secondary and excluded from the default npm test.
